key_insight: A decoupled congestion-management pipeline combining a random-forest violation detector with an actor-critic controller can robustly curtail overloads in low-voltage grids despite sparse observability and noisy measurements.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical control strategy for distribution grids facing rising PV, EV, and heat-pump loads, where safe operation must be maintained even with imperfect sensing and model uncertainty.
method: Random-forest pre-classifier flags likely grid-limit violations
Actor-critic controller computes curtailment actions for congestion mitigation
Robustness is evaluated under measurement noise and grid-parameter mismatch
evidence_signal: On a real low-voltage grid with synthetic future scenarios, the approach reduced total violation magnitude by 98.9% with accurate grid parameters and remained nearly unchanged under tested measurement-noise levels.
watch_item: Performance is more sensitive to grid-model mismatch than to measurement noise, so deployment should account for parameter uncertainty and validate against local network data.
paper_title: Robustness of Reinforcement Learning-Based Congestion Management in Low-Voltage Grids
